purpose: Auxiliary text rendered below a form input to communicate guidance (`helper`), validation errors (`invalid`), required-field reminders (`required`), or a locked/disabled state (`disabled`). Each variant changes only color (and, for `disabled`, prepends a lock icon) so the visual weight stays consistent with the field above it.
useWhen: Guidance under a bare input you compose yourself (format hints, limits).
A validation error (`kind="invalid"`), a required reminder (`kind="required"`), or a locked-field notice (`kind="disabled"`) under a field.
avoidWhen: A standard form field → use `field`, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` render this helper and wire it to the control.
The field name or required marker above the input → use `label`.
Feedback about a whole form or page rather than one field → use `message`.
related: label` — sits above the input; HelperText sits below it.
field` — `Field.Description` switches the helper `kind` from the Field's `disabled`, `invalid` and `required` state.
message` — banner-level feedback with severity and an optional action.
bestPractices: Give it an `id` and point the input's `aria-describedby` at it so screen readers read it with the field.
Pick `kind` from the field state: `invalid` for errors, `required` for a missing required value, `disabled` when the field is locked.
Keep it to one short line; `kind="disabled"` already prepends the lock icon, so do not add another.
